title: Crisis detector, Spanish
notes: TIER STAYS watch, AND THAT IS NOT A RECALL RESULT. recall_must_detect is now 1.0 over 184 must-detect rows with fp_rate_hard_negatives 0.0 over 279 and fp_rate_neutral 0.0 over 107 — every floor is met. The blocker is the one this suite has always recorded and it is an OWNER step, not an engineering one: no native speaker has reviewed the Spanish corpus, so every row still carries reviewed:false (fixtures/README.md rule 6; benchmark plan, owner-decision default 3). Gating CI on labels nobody has validated would let a mislabelled row either red a PR wrongly or, worse, freeze a wrong behaviour as a floor, so the flip waits for the review rather than for the number. B1b closed the 21 residual misses: passive_ideation 10 ('todos estarian mejor sin mi', 'ojala no despertara manana', 'no le veo sentido a nada', 'nada cambiaria si yo no estuviera', 'ojala nunca hubiera nacido', 'prefiero estar muerta que seguir asi'), explicit_intent 5 (including the one-line parity fix on the matarme entry, which lacked the 'me voy a matar' branch its English twin has had all along), means_pills 3 (guardar / contar / el botiquin entero), selfharm_cutting 2 (quemarse a proposito, 'me lastimo para sentir algo') and abuse 1 ('me lastiman en la casa'). details.recallByFamily now reports every family at 1.0; headline recall moved 0.696 -> 0.88 (B1) -> 1.0, with 23 new guard rows added in seven new benign families (ausencia_benigna, sentido_benigno, irse_benigno, acabar_benigno, carta_benigna, quemadura_accidente, lesion_accidente) and no false positive in either silent bucket. WHEN THE NATIVE REVIEW LANDS: flip tier to gate, set reviewed:true on the reviewed rows, and set the baseline with a --reason per docs/runbooks/benchmarks.md. Correct the corpus and the detector, never the floor.
